Veradermics has announced positive results from the Phase III trial of the VDPHL01 tablet for baldness.

Veradermics reported that the prolonged-release minoxidil tablet VDPHL01 met all primary and secondary endpoints in the Phase III study. The trial involved 536 men with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia.
According to the company's data, differences from placebo in hair counts, patient assessments, and investigator evaluations were seen as early as two months. By six months, non-vellus hair growth per square centimeter was 28.6 with once-daily dosing and 36.4 with twice-daily dosing compared to 6.6 with placebo. The developers stated that no serious adverse events related to the drug or cardiac events were reported.

The company plans to submit an application for approval to the FDA. If approved, this would be the first non-hormonal oral treatment for androgenetic alopecia.

⚖️ Thai Supreme Court: Bitcoin is property, thieves beware

Thailand's Supreme Court has ruled that Bitcoin qualifies as property under Thai law — after a convicted thief tried to argue otherwise to escape punishment. The court's logic was straightforward: BTC has a market price, can be cashed out, and is held by the public. That's property. The ruling upheld a 10-year sentence for a man who assisted in the robbery.

Attempting to use legal ambiguity as a get-out-of-jail-free card didn't work. If anything, the court just made the legal ground firmer for everyone — including future prosecutors.

📌 Watch-Only Wallets: Tracking Crypto Without Access to Funds

Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

🔖 Australia proposes new crypto exchange rules for 2027 

📣 Australia has proposed new rules for cryptocurrency trading and custody platforms on October 15, 2026, with financial regulator ASIC seeking public feedback by November 27 before the country’s digital asset licensing framework takes effect in April 2027. 

📊 The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) announced the consultation alongside Consultation Paper 392, which outlines planned requirements for customer asset protection, trading practices and financial resources. The regulator expects to publish final guidance in March 2027, giving businesses time to prepare for the new licensing requirements. Australia’s upcoming rules will bring more cryptocurrency businesses under the country’s existing financial services licensing framework.

⚡️ The Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 creates two regulated categories: digital asset platforms and tokenized custody platforms. Digital asset platforms hold digital tokens for customers and provide related services, while tokenized custody platforms use digital tokens to record customers’ rights to underlying assets.
